title: What the ITDR Admin Portal help describes for endpoint agents: Endpoint Settings, agent configuration, update groups, safe processes and the Client Connector for Windows deployment

{{update-group-table}} {{update-group-criteria}} {{phased-updates-effect}} {{update-group-icons}} The server agents' update groups are in [[identity-protection.server-agents]].

{{safe-process-table}} {{safe-process-configure}} {{safe-process-regex-use}} {{safe-process-internal}} Whether the process-tree option and detection types of the Deception safe-process page exist here is not stated {{gap:safe-process-controls}}.

prose.heading: Deploying with Zscaler Client Connector for Windows

prose.text: {{cc-no-separate-entitlement}} {{cc-prerequisites}} {{cc-enable-default-version}} Which Client Connector version applies differs within the page {{divergence:cc-minimum-version}}. {{deception-cc-version}}
{{cc-egress}} What each egress host carries is not stated {{gap:egress-hosts}}. {{cc-installer-sync}} {{cc-policy-verify}}

checks.do: For the Client Connector version ITDR on Windows needs, the prerequisites list and the step 1 version on the same page, and the Deception copy's own version scoped to Deception.
For which icon disables phased updates for an endpoint agent update group, the Managing page's instruction and the table's meaning of the X and Checkmark icons.
For the default installer service name, the ITDR default on this page rather than the Deception copy's default.

purpose.statement: Endpoint Settings is described as managing agent details and safe processes, customizing agent configuration and configuring phased agent updates, and as enabling an LDAP-based AD scan and a credential exposure scan on endpoints.

quotes: Endpoint Settings allow you to manage agents' details and safe processes, customize agent configuration, and configure phased updates for agents.
Trigger an LDAP-based AD scan to communicate with the AD domain and identify vulnerabilities.
Trigger a credential exposure scan on endpoints to detect exposed credentials and other identity-related data that can be easily exfiltrated.

cpu-cap.statement: The Endpoint Settings page states that the endpoint agent's CPU consumption is capped at 25%.

quotes: The endpoint agent's CPU consumption is capped at 25%.

agents-table-columns.statement: The Agents table lists, for each system, System Name, System User Name, Client Connector User, Matched Policies (threat detection policies applied on the endpoint), First Seen (when the agent was installed), Last Seen (when it last connected to the ITDR Admin Portal), OS Version, Version, the endpoint credential exposure policy name and status, and IP.

quotes: System Name: The name of the system.
System User Name: The usernames of the system.
Client Connector User: The usernames in Zscaler Client Connector.
Matched Policies: The threat detection policies that are applied on the endpoint.
First Seen: The date and time when the agent was installed on the system.
Last Seen: The date and time when the agent was last connected to the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
OS Version: The operating system (OS) name and version.
Version: The endpoint agent version number.
Endpoint Credential Exposure Policy Name: The name of the endpoint credential exposure policy on the endpoint agent.
IP: The IP address of the system.

credex-policy-status.statement: The Endpoint Credential Exposure Policy Status column shows values such as Completed Successfully, Completed Partially, Failed, Processing and Not Started, and clicking Failed or Completed Partially opens the error logs, which show Timestamp, Type, Message and Detail.

quotes: The status of the endpoint credential exposure policy (e.g., Completed Successfully, Completed Partially, Failed, Processing, Not Started).
you can view the logs of the error by clicking the Failed or Completed Partially status.
Timestamp: The date and timestamp for when the error was generated.
Type: The type of endpoint credential exposure policy.
Detail: The detailed description of the error.
Message: The message of the error.

show-all-agents.statement: Inactive agents are endpoint agents with a last check-in time older than 7 days; the Show all agents option in the Actions menu is disabled by default and, when disabled, only active agents are displayed.

quotes: Inactive agents are the endpoint agents with last check-in time older than 7 days.
By default, this setting is disabled.
If disabled, only active agents are displayed.

troubleshooter-error-logs.statement: The Agents tab offers a Troubleshooter download for managing endpoint agents with CLI commands, and error logs are generated when a critical event occurs on the agent, with a View Error Logs icon showing the latest log entry.

quotes: Download Troubleshooter to manage the endpoint agents using CLI commands.
When a critical event occurs on the agent, error logs are generated. Click the View Error Logs icon to open the Error Logs window and view the latest log entry.

export-config.statement: Endpoint agent configuration details can be exported as CSV or JSON for all agents or filtered agents; the all-agents options export only the agents shown in the table, so Show all agents must be selected to include inactive agents, and the filters cover system name, user, policy, operating system version, ITDR Admin Portal version and IP address.

quotes: You can export endpoint agent configuration details as a CSV or JSON file.

You can export the configuration details of all the endpoint agents, or filter the agents based on the system name, user, policy, operating system version, Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal version, and IP address.
The All agents as CSV and All agents as JSON options export only the agents that are shown in the agents table.
If you want to export all agents including the inactive agents, make sure the Show all agents option is selected.

policy-details-ad-modules.statement: The threat detection policy details view for a system shows the policy name and the status (True if enabled, False if disabled) of the AD threat detection modules DCSync, DCShadow, Zerologon, Session Enumeration, Monitored Privileged Accounts, Kerberoast Detection and LDAP Detection.

quotes: The policy name and the status (True if enabled, False if disabled) of the following AD threat detection modules:
- DCSync
- DCShadow
- Zerologon
- Session Enumeration
- Monitored Privileged Accounts
- Kerberoast Detection
- LDAP Detection

agent-logs-download.statement: Triggering logs from Actions > Trigger Logs makes a Download icon appear under the agent's Actions column after a few minutes, and the logs download as a compressed .zip file.

quotes: After a few minutes, a Download icon appears under the Actions column of the selected agent.
The endpoint agent logs from the endpoint are downloaded to your system in a compressed (.zip) file.
Click Actions > Trigger Logs.

uninstall-modes.statement: Uninstall makes the agent remove the policies from the endpoint, trying for up to three days, before uninstalling itself; Force Uninstall removes the policies on a best-effort basis and then uninstalls itself.

quotes: Uninstall: The agent removes the policies from the endpoint, and then it uninstalls itself. The agent tries to remove the policies for up to three days before uninstalling itself.
Force Uninstall: The agent uninstalls the policies from the endpoint on a best-effort basis, and then it uninstalls itself.

delete-agent.statement: Endpoint agents cannot be deleted if their Last Seen value is less than 7 days.

quotes: Endpoint agents cannot be deleted if their Last Seen value is less than 7 days.

installer-defaults.statement: The Installer Customizations section sets the endpoint agent service Name (default ZSAITDR), Display name (default Zscaler ITDR) and Description, to prevent the agent from being fingerprinted; the service name should be unique and existing service names checked beforehand.

quotes: Customize the agent configuration such as name, display name, and description of the endpoint service to prevent the agent from being fingerprinted.
Edit the endpoint agent service name. The default name is ZSAITDR.
Edit the endpoint agent service display name. The default display name is Zscaler ITDR.
The endpoint agent service name should be unique.
make sure to check the names of the services running in the systems where you want to install the endpoint agents before configuring the service name.

auto-cleanup.statement: Auto-Cleanup Duplicate Agents deletes endpoint agents with duplicate hostnames from the ITDR Admin Portal, retaining the most recently connected hostnames and those connected for less than 7 days; agents deleted this way are not uninstalled from the system.

quotes: Enable the auto-cleanup to automatically delete endpoint agents with duplicate hostnames from the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal. The most recently connected hostnames and the ones that are connected for less than 7 days are retained.
Endpoint agents deleted via auto-cleanup are not uninstalled from the system. You have to manually uninstall them.

update-group-table.statement: The Agent Update Groups table lists each group's Name, Selection Criterion, Update Progress (the total number of agents updated in the group) and Update Enabled (X icon for disabled, checkmark icon for enabled).

quotes: Selection Criterion: The selection criterion specified for the agent update group.
Update Progress: The total number of agents updated in the group.
The X icon indicates that the updates are disabled for the group, and the Checkmark icon indicates that the updates are enabled for the group.
Name: The name of the agent update group.
Update Enabled: The status of phased updates.

update-group-criteria.statement: An agent update group selects endpoint agents by Hostname List (exact match with the listed hostnames) or Hostname RegEx (match against a regular expression), and Zscaler recommends an enabled catch-all "All systems" group with the expression .* after testing so all endpoints are upgraded.

quotes: Hostname List: Applies updates to all the agents where the hostname of the system exactly matches the hostnames specified in the Hostname List text box.
Hostname RegEx: Applies updates to all the agents where the hostname of the system matches the hostname pattern specified as a regular expression in the Hostname RegEx text box.
Zscaler recommends that you add a group named “All systems” with a catch-all regular expression ( .* ), and enable this group after you complete the testing to make sure all endpoints are upgraded.

phased-updates-effect.statement: Enable Phased Updates on the Agent Update Groups tab stops any automatic updates for endpoint agents that are not part of a group; group update status downloads as CSV and a group's hostnames export as a TXT file.

quotes: Enabling this feature stops any automatic updates for endpoint agents that are not a part of the groups.
A CSV file with the agent group update status is downloaded to your system.
A TXT file containing the list of hostnames is downloaded to your system.

update-group-icons.statement: On the endpoint Agent Update Groups page, the page says to click the X icon under the Actions column to disable phased updates for a group and the Checkmark icon to enable them.

quotes: Under the Actions column, click the X icon to disable phased updates, or click the Checkmark icon to enable phased updates.

safe-process-table.statement: The Safe Processes table lists Name, Enabled, Executable File Path (absolute), Executable File Regex, Executable File Hash (for example md5, sha1 and sha256), Certificate Issuer, Certificate Serial, Certificate Thumbprint and Type, where internal safe processes carry an Internal label; internal ones are predesignated by Zscaler ITDR and can be shown or hidden.

quotes: Executable File Path: The executable file path expressed in absolute values.
Executable File Regex: The executable file path expressed in regular expressions.
Executable File Hash: The executable file hash (e.g., md5, sha1, and sha256).
Certificate Issuer: A unique certificate issuer name that identifies the issuer of the digital certificate.
The internal safe processes are identified using the Internal label.
These are a set of predesignated safe processes that are provided by Zscaler ITDR.
Name: A unique identifier to categorize the safe processes.
Enabled: Shows whether a safe process is enabled or disabled.
Certificate Serial: A unique certificate serial number issued by a certificate authority.
Certificate Thumbprint: A unique certificate thumbprint that is a hash of a certificate.
Type: Shows whether a safe process is internal or not.
Show or hide internal safe processes.

safe-process-configure.statement: A safe process takes a unique Name, a Selection Type of Executable File Path (absolute) or Executable Path Regex, and an executable file hash, certificate issuer, serial and thumbprint; marking trusted processes as safe prevents generating false positives.

quotes: Marking trusted processes as safe prevents generating false positives.
Name: Enter a unique identifier for the safe process (e.g., notepad++).
If you want to use an absolute path value, select Executable File Path from the drop-down menu
If you want to use regular expression for the path value, select Executable Path Regex from the drop-down menu
Executable File Hash: Enter the executable file hash
Certificate Serial: Enter the certificate serial number
Certificate Thumbprint: Enter the certificate thumbprint
Certificate Issuer: Enter the certificate issuer name

safe-process-regex-use.statement: Regular expressions can be used for path values when the processes to be marked safe have names with a predictable string of characters, such as a version number; the page's regex example is *mcafee.*\.exe.

quotes: You can use regular expressions for path values if the processes that you want to mark as safe have names with a predictable string of characters, such as a version number.
(e.g., *mcafee.*\.exe)

safe-process-internal.statement: For internal safe processes only enabling or disabling is supported, and internal safe processes cannot be deleted.

quotes: For internal safe processes, only the option to enable or disable is supported.
Internal safe processes cannot be deleted.

cc-no-separate-entitlement.statement: The Client Connector deployment page states that ITDR uses Deception configuration because there is no separate service entitlement for ITDR in Zscaler Client Connector, and that there is no separate ITDR UI in the Client Connector Portal.

quotes: ITDR uses Deception configuration because there is no separate service entitlement for ITDR in Zscaler Client Connector.
ITDR uses Deception configuration and there is no separate UI for ITDR in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.

cc-prerequisites.statement: The prerequisites for deploying ITDR with Client Connector for Windows are SSO configured in ZIA, Client Connector at 4.3.0.264, 4.4.0.383 or 4.5.0.344 or later, and ITDR capabilities enabled on Client Connector by contacting the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: Configured SSO in ZIA.
4.3.0.264 or later
4.4.0.383 or later
4.5.0.344 or later
Enabled ITDR capabilities on your Zscaler Client Connector by contacting your Zscaler Account team.

cc-egress.statement: The Client Connector prerequisites require outbound HTTPS access from the proxy and/or firewall to the ITDR Admin Portal on port 443 (<your_subdomain>.illusionblack.com) and to dwv281inkfqg3.cloudfront.net on port 443.

quotes: Outbound HTTPS access from either or both of your proxy and firewall in your local environment to:
Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal on port 443, i.e., <your_subdomain>.illusionblack.com on port 443
dwv281inkfqg3.cloudfront.net on port 443

cc-enable-default-version.statement: Step 1 says to enable Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default in the Client Connector Portal to enable ITDR for all Client Connector users upgraded to 3.9 or later for Windows, or to disable it and select a group from the User Groups drop-down menu to enable ITDR for a specific group of users.

quotes: Enable Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default to enable ITDR for all Zscaler Client Connector users upgraded to 3.9 or later for Windows.
If you want to enable ITDR for a specific group of users, disable Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default, and then select a group from the User Groups drop-down menu.
Step 1: Enable ITDR in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal

deception-cc-version.statement: The Deception copy of the Client Connector for Windows deployment page says to enable Deception for users upgraded to Deception version 4.6 or later for Windows.

quotes: upgraded to Deception version 4.6 or later for Windows

cc-installer-sync.statement: Step 2 customizes the endpoint installer Name, Display Name and Description in the ITDR Admin Portal under Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agent Configuration to prevent fingerprinting, and step 3 says to click Zscaler Deception in the left-side navigation and click Sync if the Zscaler Deception installer settings (Name, Display Name and Description) shown on that page do not match the values entered.

quotes: Customize the Name, Display Name, and Description of the endpoint installer or service to prevent the agent from being fingerprinted.
If they don't match, click Sync to get the latest values.
Log in to the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
Go to Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agent Configuration.
Verify if the Zscaler Deception installer settings (Name, Display Name, and Description) you see on this page match the settings you entered in the previous step.
In the left-side navigation, click Zscaler Deception.

cc-policy-verify.statement: Step 4 requires the Logout Password, Exit Password and Password to access Deception Settings in the Windows policy, and step 5 verifies the configuration by entering that password in Advanced Settings, after which the Service Status is Running.

quotes: enter the Logout Password, Exit Password, and Password to access Deception Settings.
The configuration is successful and the Service Status is Running.
Enter the password you created in the previous step.
After the app update is complete, click Advanced Settings.

cc-minimum-version.summary: The ITDR Client Connector for Windows page lists 4.3.0.264, 4.4.0.383 and 4.5.0.344 as prerequisites, and its step 1 refers to users upgraded to 3.9 or later.

quotes: 4.3.0.264 or later
4.4.0.383 or later
4.5.0.344 or later

positions.says: The prerequisites list Client Connector 4.3.0.264, 4.4.0.383 or 4.5.0.344 or later.

quotes: Enable Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default to enable ITDR for all Zscaler Client Connector users upgraded to 3.9 or later for Windows.

positions.says: Step 1 enables ITDR for all Client Connector users upgraded to 3.9 or later for Windows.

cc-minimum-version.impact: The page gives two minimum Client Connector versions for ITDR on Windows and does not say which applies.

safe-process-controls.title: Whether the process-tree option and detection types of the Deception safe-process page exist in ITDR
safe-process-controls.detail: The ITDR safe-process pages have no OS selector, process-tree option or Detection Type and Subtype tables; whether ITDR has those controls or only omits them from the page is not stated.

egress-hosts.title: What each egress host in the Client Connector prerequisites carries
egress-hosts.detail: The prerequisites name the ITDR Admin Portal subdomain on illusionblack.com and dwv281inkfqg3.cloudfront.net on port 443 without saying what each carries.
